newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Merger, buyback news key for Royal.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Merger, buyback news key for Royal.

text.p: News about progress on last year's merger and the timing of the share buyback announced in March are likely to be the main focus of attention when British composite insurer Royal & Sun Alliance reports first quarter results next Tuesday.

At the time of the 1996 results, management emphasised the company was on target to achieve at least the 175 million pounds annual savings forecast when the six billion pound merger of Royal Insurance and Sun Alliance Insurance was announced last May.
Over 1,500 staff have gone since then with middle mangement being cut by one third. Around 5,000 jobs are likely to go in all.
The costs of the restructuring in 1996 were 201 million pounds, some 40 million pounds more than analysts had expected.
The annnual results also heralded the announcement of a buyback of five percent of Royal Sun's shares, the first by a British insurance company.
That was approved at the company's annual meeting last week. No announcement on timing has been made but the shares cannot be bought in until the first quarter figures on May 20.
There have been hints that the buyback, initiated in anticipation of continued strengthening in its capital position, could be repeated in the future.
At the AGM the company also predicted the first quarter would show an improvement over last year which was affected by severe weather losses in the U.S.
For the year as a whole, weather costs depressed profits by some 94 million pounds.
Milder winter weather has helped General Accident and Commercial Union, both of whom have posted results in the last few days, to report a rebound in profits from last year's depressed levels.
No figures for the first quarter were announced last year but pro forma figures released at the AGM put the 1996 pre-tax operating profit at 157 million pounds.
Analysts are forecasting this year's operating profits at between 170 and 195 million pounds.
Last year's poorly performing UK private motor business is likely to remain under pressure although rival insurers have said in recent days that some firming in motor rates is beginning to be seen.
Royal Sun expressed confidence at the annual results that motor rates had bottomed and was scheduling increases for this year.

On a more negative note, both General Accident and Commercial Union have reported sharp increases in subsidence in the first quarter, blaming the dry start to the year and increased turnover in the housing market.
Royal Sun is Britain's largest house structure insurer and of the group's global non-life premium income, 14 percent is accounted for by UK household business.
According to some analysts there is nervousness about the group's intention to make acquisitions, particularly to build up its European life operations.
At the year end, it played down the possibility of a large acquisition, emphasising that the focus was on integration.
In April it announced the acquisition of Prudential's life assurance and pensions business in Italy for 46 million pounds.
The price involved goodwill of around 19 million pounds.
The business, which last year earned premium income of 52 million pounds, will be put together with its own life arm in Italy where turnover was 13 million pounds.
-- Simon Cowell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7721
